newsitem.title: FRANCE: French grain market quiet, wheat loads for Iraq.
newsitem.headline: French grain market quiet, wheat loads for Iraq.

text.p: French grain markets eased slowly back into gear on Monday after a two-week break, with most prices unchanged from pre-Christmas levels, traders said.
The highlight in wheat was the start of loadings to Iraq at Rouen under a United Nations oil-for-food pact that has seen sales from France of at least 300,000 tonnes.
Precise details of shipments were not immediately available.
Wheat was unchanged from year-end levels at 860-865 francs per tonne at Rouen excluding carrying charges, brokers said.
Iraq bought 300,000 tonnes of French wheat, as well as about 100,000 tonnes from Australia, shortly after limited oil exports began under a six-month U.N. deal in the week of December 16.
Traders said the recent spell of sub-zero temperatures in northwest Europe had sparked some extra demand for wheat deliveries by truck to northern Europe after canals froze.
"But (the volumes) are not significant," one broker said.
In barley, attention focused on a new Saudi purchase tender for 1.2 million tonnes to be delivered in February and March.
Most of the barley is expected to come from the European Union with extra sales coming from Australia and Canada.
Saudi Arabia earlier announced a December 7 tender for 1.2 million tonnes of optional-origin barley.
The tender calls for 500,000 tonnes to arrive by the end of February and a further 700,000 tonnes by March 30.
French barley was a touch firmer at 860 francs excluding transport costs for delivery in northern ports in January or February.
MATIF French barge wheat futures were flat at 883 francs per tonne on volume of 16 lots for May, the only month traded.
